newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA sets $1.0 bln share buyback.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA sets $1.0 bln share buyback.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp said Tuesday its board has authorized a $1.0 billion stock repurchase program.
At the same time, the company said it and Value Health, Inc have signed an amended and restated merger agreement in which Columbia would pay $20.50 in cash for each Value Health common share.
At current trading prices, the shares to be bought back under the program would represent approximately five percent of Columbia/HCA's $21 billion market capitalization.
The repurchases would be made in the open market from time to time, said Richard Scott, chairman and chief executive officer of Columbia.
The time-frame for the stock repurchase program will depend upon market conditions and repurchased shares will be held as treasury stock and be available for general corporate purposes, he said.

He said that with Columbia's strong cash flow and strong balance sheet, the company can carry out the repurchase and still pay $1.1 billion in cash to purchase Value Health shares while continuing with capital reinvestments, acquisitions, joint ventures, and construction of additional hospitals.
